report:
Reviewed the complete normalization_demand claim, three ordinary implementation associations, explicit implementation TODO, both substantive associated tests, and the TODO test. This is a mixed implemented/deferred assessment, not a claim of full destination implementation.

Requirements: aliases retain identity until explicit demand; revealability belongs to canonical inputs; projection demand is restricted to the fixed trait/item, applicable headers, selected values and necessary predicates; unrelated impls and bodies are excluded. solve_query dispatches Normalize explicitly. solve_normalize_frame accepts associated aliases with empty GAT arguments, otherwise returns Maybe; it matches candidate heads and proves candidate predicates before load_prepared_associated_value, so rejected candidates do not fetch values. The latter uses the selected impl/item key for local or external lookup. local_impl_associated_type_value selects one named type item through local_impl_associated_item, lowers only its type and owner generics, rejects unsupported generics/predicates/attributes, and never requests a checked body. Candidate predicates are header predicates, not executable bodies. The keyed producer examines member identities but lowers only the selected member. These are meaningful ordinary implementation slices.

The local_normalization_reads_one_keyed_value_without_impl_item_enumeration test visibly constructs two same-trait candidates with differing trait arguments and sibling associated types; it asserts successful normalization, exactly one value query and keyed member query, absence of aggregate impl-items lowering, warm reuse, and unchanged selected-value reuse after a sibling-value edit. It also checks reuse when aggregate enumeration previously populated the canonical item producer. These assertions detect premature value loading for rejected headers and sibling-value dependencies. nested_associated_value_remains_a_normalizable_alias asserts that normalizing Outer::Item yields the still-identifiable Inner::Value alias, then independently normalizes the latter to i32. This verifies demand preserves nested alias identity instead of eagerly expanding its value. Setup helpers only construct a fixture and locate trait/item identities; outcome assertions are visible in the tests.

Deferrals are explicit and justified: canonical folding preserves named/opaque identities, but canonical GoalQueryData construction has no reveal-context field and normalization only supports associated aliases. Named alias expansion and opaque reveal-context behavior therefore remain implementation TODO, with inside/outside opaque results and reveal-preserving round trips deferred until that representation and operation exist. Local candidate discovery still scans local impl CST/trait identities; its exclusion of unrelated impl reads is NOT implemented. The TODO now names the tracked private index prerequisite specified by local_index_firewall, preserving the ordinary selected-value behavior rather than reclassifying it. The TODO test also retains the full demand matrix (external/local header/value/body tracing and all alias round trips); its empty body is not passing behavioral evidence. Current ordinary tests establish the narrower local selected-value and associated-identity slice, not universal no-body/no-unrelated-impl traces. No N/A entries exist.

Added essential implementation associations in clauses.rs and local_syms/impls.rs and associated the two existing substantive tests. No production behavior changed. After edits ran cargo fmt, then cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib normalization_reads_one_keyed_value -- --nocapture and cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib nested_associated_value_remains_a_normalizable_alias -- --nocapture; each executed one passing test. Fresh start captured the edited inputs. Additional dependency reads capture canonical construction/folding, keyed member producer, external selected-value query, local-index specification, and fixture helpers. This review does not claim execution of deferred tests or external integration tests. Workspace build and centralized post-codegen/sanity review are assigned to the coordinator. No additional edits are requested for this review of the implemented slice and explicitly retained architecture deferrals.
